original.note: Other concurrent edits appeared in the main worktree during continuation and were preserved; only performance worktree files were edited for this stage.

changes: Export the existing cost-role catalog and reuse its complete ID/name map for fallback RDO costing, allocated attendance and monthly diagnosis.
Select current/history role IDs and effective dates instead of reading nested JobRole relations again. Point calculation now shares the same pure hydration helper.
Preserve source/history order, effective dates, cost exclusions, names without profiles, and supplied legacy relations when an adapter lacks role IDs. No input mutation.
Group cost catalog remains lazy and request-owned; access/category/project/division guards and identity source order remain unchanged.
No new cross-request cache, concurrency limit, pool setting, index, migration or financial formula.

comparisonDesign.method: Synthetic loopback HTTP against real Express and migrated PostgreSQL, persisted hashed sessions, body receipt included. No proxy, TLS, rendering, external API or production load.
comparisonDesign.database: PostgreSQL 16, one CPU, 768 MiB. Eight API connections, four concurrent requests, summary point projection, distributed reports across two members.
comparisonDesign.order: Control, candidate, then candidate, control; cohorts ran sequentially, without tests or concurrent benchmark workloads during timing. API host not isolated.
comparisonDesign.counts: Per cohort: 800 warm responses (100 per route/profile), eight first-process responses, eight warmups, 16 after-write responses; eight expected auth/module negatives separately.
comparisonDesign.sourceParity: Separate baseline/candidate processes read exactly the same PostgreSQL rows. Eight complete normalized outputs compared before/after role name, salary and report-hour writes. Includes role history without profiles, overlapping imports, outside-point RDO costs, planned hours and day/night allocation.

ci.appliesTo: Pushed be1fad15 only; not the local role-catalog continuation.

backendSuite.databaseOptIns: Dedicated PostgreSQL opt-ins disabled in full suite and exercised separately.

focused.note: Initial focused run; final missing-ID compatibility assertion was subsequently covered in the complete suite.

validation.syntax: Changed application modules and helper passed node --check; git diff --check passed.
validation.frontend: No frontend changes. Pushed baseline CI includes frontend tests, lint, build, budgets and browser regressions.
validation.cleanup: No fixture projects outside the two bootstrap internal projects, reports, collaborators, imports, users, sessions, groups or synthetic role/profile rows remained. Bootstrap roles/profiles are expected. The owned disposable PostgreSQL container and volumes were removed after validation.

acceptance.queryReduction: Two calls per affected attendance/diagnosis/direct detail/group/division calculation; two per warm HTTP detail/group response (53-54 to 51-52). Point remains 36, cards remain 11.
acceptance.latency: Sequential cohorts on an unisolated API host are descriptive, not a causal or statistical latency acceptance. Retained improvement is proven redundant-query removal with complete result parity.

limitations: One fresh-process sample per route/profile per cohort does not support cold p95 or the general cold reduction target. Database pages are warm and process imports excluded.
Pool samples are active-interval observations, not per-query queue durations. Submitted-query peaks include queries waiting for a connection.
After-write timings start after confirmed commit and measurement setup; cards retain normal cache expiry.
